title: The lane-archive refusal names the add_repo act when it cannot read a lane's repo
why: lane-closes-after-records refused three times tonight on lane session-mailbox-followups because this session could not read the lane's second repo; add_repo fixed it at 09:08 CST. The owner asked (09:12 CST) that the fix be mechanical.
source: retrospective 09:13 CST Nov 13, owner ask 09:12 CST
note: Fix: when the archive guard cannot read a lane repo, its refusal names the act 'add_repo <owner>/<repo> (read), then retry', with the repo from the lane's cs-repo tag. Red first: a fixture lane whose repo read fails gets that remedy. The gap itself (archive-guard-child-repo-read) is a debt for the lane to file on main. 13:14 CST Nov 17 (coordinator relay, filed by triage 11): hook lane-closes-after-records refused archive_session twice, "the open pull requests of the lane's repo (shivinate7/mailaudit) could not be read". Measured by the coordinator: add_repo access read attaches nothing for a public repo, so the guard's gh could not read its PRs; access push fixed it. So the planned remedy text must say access push, not (read), and the guard could read a public repo's open PRs anonymously over REST. The owner asked how to resolve this mechanically (13:10 CST); page item 937 asks which of three fixes. Do not build past the text change until it is answered.
